question: Which of Run's contract lines does each security blocker comment raise, over the M13 working set?

source.workingSet: the 1,001 security blocker comments of docs/evidence/blocks/2026-09-17-review-blockers.json (maintainer comments on omacom/omarchy-plugin-marketplace, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-17)

method: Each security blocker comment was asked one yes/no question per requirement by a calibrated classification model that returns a probability per option; yes at probability 0.5 or higher. The question: Does this comment raise the requirement, as a blocker or required fix, anywhere in it (yes at probability 0.5 or higher). A comment can raise several requirements, so the counts overlap and do not sum to the comment count. The working set and the scripts that ran the questions are not committed: they quote review text about named plugins.

requirements.absolute_executable: an executable, interpreter or helper is resolved by bare name through PATH, through #!/usr/bin/env, a login shell, or a user-writable fallback location, instead of a fixed absolute path
requirements.closed_environment: a child process inherits the ambient environment (for example PATH, BASH_ENV, PYTHONPATH, LD_PRELOAD, shell startup files) instead of a cleared, minimal, explicit environment
requirements.argv_not_shell_string: a command is built as a shell string (bash -c, sh -c, string interpolation into a command line) instead of an argv array of separate arguments
requirements.hard_deadline: a started process has no absolute deadline or timeout, or a timeout that does not reliably end it
requirements.group_teardown: terminating a process does not end its descendants or process group (TERM then KILL to the whole group), so children can survive, hold pipes, or keep running
requirements.reap_order_and_pid_identity: a process is signalled by a stored or reused PID or process-group number, or the leader is reaped before the group cleanup finished, so a signal can hit an unrelated process
requirements.output_cap_while_reading: stdout, stderr or another stream is collected without a byte or line limit enforced while reading (for example StdioCollector, reading all output, clipping only after exit)
requirements.cancel_on_destruction: a running process is not cancelled and cleaned up when its component is destroyed, reloaded, or superseded by a newer run
requirements.untrusted_output_display: process output or error text is shown or notified without being treated as plain text with a length bound

limits: One reviewer account and 6.7 days; a policy change moves every share.

A count is the model's reading of the reviewer's wording against the requirement's text, not the marketplace's taxonomy; hand spot checks in the M13 classification found the runner judgment generous, so read each count as an upper bound.
A comment raising a requirement is not resolved by a block that implements it; the block handles the plumbing, the review decides.
